item.title: Digital Archive Services
item.description: Open Access - the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives Welcome to the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives. These records include bills introduced in the Legislature, reports from the Governor's Executive Council, election returns, deeds and maps from the Maine Land Office, vital statistics prior to 1892, federal census records up to 1880, county court records dating back to 1636, and military records through World War I, among others. As of March 1, 2026, our online collection includes over one million individual records. The Maine State Archives will continue to expand this database as we digitize more of our collection. All documents are public records and are free to download.
item.content:encoded:
Open Access - the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives

Welcome to the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives. These records include bills introduced in the Legislature, reports from the Governor's Executive Council, election returns, deeds and maps from the Maine Land Office, vital statistics prior to 1892, federal census records up to 1880, county court records dating back to 1636, and military records through World War I, among others. As of March 1, 2026, our online collection includes over one million individual records. The Maine State Archives will continue to expand this database as we digitize more of our collection. All documents are public records and are free to download.

item.title: BNC Notice & Service Disruption
item.description: Thursday, October 15, 2026 The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors. The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF. At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. Additionally, the following websites are unavailable: bnc.uscourts.gov bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov notices.uscourts.gov National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, October 15, 2026

The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors.

The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF.

At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. 

Additionally, the following websites are unavailable:

  • bnc.uscourts.gov
  • bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov
  • notices.uscourts.gov
  • National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels

The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.

item.title: Seal Cove Auto Museum v. John J. Sanford et al.
item.description:
MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT Reporter of Decisions Decision: 2026 ME 110 Docket: BCD-25-555 Argued: October 8, 2026 Decided: November 19, 2026
Panel: STANFILL, C.J., and MEAD, CONNORS, DOUGLAS, and LIPEZ, JJ.
SEAL COVE AUTO MUSEUM
v.
JOHN J. SANFORD et al.
LIPEZ, J. [¶1] In 2020, the parties to this appeal, Seal Cove Auto Museum , the Richard C. Paine, Jr., Automobile Collection Charitable Trust (the Trust or the Charitable Trust), and the Trust’s trustees, John J. Sanford and John Peabody Monks Higgins (the Trustees) , entered into a settlement agreement and an amended relationship agreement to resolve a legal dispute. In 2022, after the Trust announced a plan to donate $1,000,000 to the Owls Head Transportation Museum, Seal Cove filed a motion to enforce, arguing that the donation to Owls Head violated the Trust’s and the Trustees’ obligations under the agreements. After a bench trial, t he Business and Consumer Docket ( Duddy, J.) denied the motion, and Seal Cove now appeals, primarily asserting that the trial court misinterpreted relevant provisions of the amended relationship agreement and
2 erred in finding that the Trust had not breached that agreement. Upon review of Seal Cove’s arguments, we conclude that they lack merit, and we accordingly affirm. I. BACKGROUND [¶2] This is not the first time that we have addressed an appeal involving these parties. As we explained in Attorney General v. Sanford: Richard Paine Jr. established Seal Cove in 1963 and the Richard C. Paine, Jr., Automobile Collection Charitable Trust (the Trust) in 1986. The Trust and Seal Cove were established to maintain and display Paine ’s large collection of antique automobiles. Following Paine's death in 2007, the Trust acquired most of Paine ’s automobiles and an endowment to support maintenance and display of the automobile collection. Sanford and Higgins presently serve as trustees of the Trust.

item.title: Calendar Year 2027 Home Health Prospective Payment System (HH PPS) Rate Update; Requirements for the HH Quality Reporting Program and the Expanded HH Value-Based Purchasing Model; Medicare Provider Enrollment, Durable Medical Equipment (DME), and DME, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies (DMEPOS) Policies
item.description: This final rule sets forth routine updates to the Medicare home health payment rates in accordance with existing statutory and regulatory requirements. In addition, this final rule discusses the behavior adjustments and finalizes a temporary behavior adjustment. It also finalizes the recalibrated case-mix weights and updated functional impairment levels; comorbidity subgroups; and low-utilization payment adjustment (LUPA) thresholds for CY 2027. Additionally, this final rule discusses and responds to comments on the provision of home health palliative care services and includes a summary of comments received on the request for information (RFI) on a home health specific wage index included in the proposed rule. This rule also finalizes changes to the Home Health Quality Reporting Program (HH QRP) and summarizes potential initiatives to improve alignment between the HH QRP and expanded Home Health Value- Based Purchasing (HHVBP) Model. Lastly, the rule clarifies the application of the DMEPOS face-to- face encounter requirements for the replacement of DMEPOS items; makes changes to the provider and supplier enrollment requirements; makes changes to implement a DME benefit expansion for infusion pumps and drugs; and discusses collection of information requirement changes regarding the DMEPOS Competitive Bidding Program (CBP) country of origin.
